subject: SLA: tailored archival-hold & staggered purge cadence for CalyxBio
messages:
From: procurement@calyxbio.com
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bespoke retention windows & deletion timelines - initial ask
Cc: techops@calyxbio.com

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking the time earlier. As we discussed, CalyxBio needs an SLA and order form language that covers a few non-standard residency/retention items for regulated datasets: 1) a staggered purge cadence for derivative artifacts (30/90/180 days depending on dataset class), 2) an archival-hold capability where records can be held beyond the retention window for legal holds, and 3) a verifiable deletion certificate at end-of-life for datasets and backups.

Attached is our current data policy (CalyxDataPolicy.pdf) and a short table of dataset classes. Can you outline how Redwood would map those to retention windows, the deletion proof you provide, and whether we can include a 90-day temporary extension for forensic holds that is reversible by our Security team?

Appreciate a short proposal and any sample order form language we can send to procurement/legal.

Regards,

Procurement Team
CalyxBio

Attachment: CalyxDataPolicy.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: procurement@calyxbio.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bespoke retention windows & deletion timelines - initial ask
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Hi Calyx team,

Thanks for the clear summary and the policy doc. High-level responses below; I attached our SLA template with inline comments (redwood-sla-template.pdf) and a starting order form Exhibit A.

- Staggered purge cadence: We can support per-dataset-class retention windows (e.g., 30/90/180) and implement automatic tiered purges. We'll surface these as Exhibit A in the order form where you can map dataset classes to windows.
- Archival-hold (for legal/forensic): We support a reversible hold flag that pauses scheduled deletion. Holds are scoped to dataset IDs and require an authorized request from your Security team. Holds can be time-bound or indefinite; suggested default maximum reversible hold is 90 days unless you request an extension with an administrative approval process.
- Deletion proof: We provide a machine-readable deletion certificate with SHA256 of object manifests and a deletion timestamp; for backups or replicated replicas we provide proofs per-replica. We can also provide an attestation PDF signed by Redwood Ops for contract purposes.

Open questions for you: 1) Do you need a hard maximum on how long holds may remain reversible before escalation? 2) Do you expect certs to include per-shard proof (we can include) or is a per-dataset manifest fine?

Looping Monica and Karthik on follow-ups — Monica for technical execution, Karthik for order form & legal language.

Next step: Monica will propose the exact Exhibit A mapping and a short runbook for hold requests. Once we align, Karthik can produce a redlined order form for your legal.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Bespoke retention windows & deletion timelines - technical mapping

Hi team,

Thanks — below is a practical mapping and operational notes based on your dataset classes in CalyxDataPolicy.pdf. I kept the language intentionally concrete so it can flow into Exhibit A.

Proposed per-class mapping (example):
- PII/PHI variants: primary retention = 30 days, archival hold eligible (90-day reversible hold), permanent deletion after hold expiry + 7-day verification window.
- Derived research artifacts: primary retention = 90 days, archival hold eligible (60-day reversible hold), staggered purge of derivative caches at 30 days, full object deletion at 90 days.
- Aggregated analytics outputs: primary retention = 180 days, no reversible hold by default (optional add-on).

Operational details and constraints:
- Holds are applied via an authenticated API call and create an immutable hold record (who requested, ticket id). Only designated Calyx Security roles can clear holds. We can integrate with your Identity provider for role checks.
- Deletion certificate: after purge completes we publish a signed manifest (SHA256 list) and a human-readable attestation. If you require, we can route these to an S3 bucket you own or push via webhook.
- Backups/replicas: Purge operations include secondary replicas; timeline for replicated deletion is configurable but default is synchronous within the same compliance window.
- Forensic extension: we can implement a one-time 90-day forensic extension that requires a signed acceptance form and will be visible in Console as an Outstanding Hold with an expiry.

Edge cases:
- Emergency legal holds: we can convert reversible holds to indefinite holds, but that will require an escalation flow (email + ticket) and will be billed as an ad-hoc operational request in the order form.
- Material scope changes: if dataset class counts exceed thresholds in Exhibit A we will recalibrate throughput/retention costs.

I can convert this into Exhibit A wording (table + API examples) — sending a draft in 2 hours.

— Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sara — attaching an initial redline of Exhibit A and the order form with specific billing callouts (see redlines-kiyer-20260826.pdf). A few legal notes:

- We included explicit language for reversible holds and the forensic 90-day extension. The reversible hold section includes an approval workflow and a cost schedule for hold processing.
- Deletion attestation: We added contract language requiring Redwood to produce a signed deletion attestation within 10 business days of purge completion.
- SLA credits: We added a carve-out so that holds do not count against uptime/availability SLOs but do factor into data-handling response SLAs.

Action items for Calyx: please confirm the list of Security roles that can clear holds and whether you want deletion certificates pushed to your S3 bucket (we'll need a bucket ARN and write role).

I'll stand by to incorporate your redlines.
